title: Integrated rehearsal playground with telemetry fuzzing and safety harness
author: Maya Chen
description: Adds a confined oncall rehearsal playground for replaying recent incidents and running safe experiments against sanitized telemetry. Motivation: teams need a low-friction way to rehearse runbooks and validate mitigations without touching production state or leaking PII. This PR introduces a sandboxed playback engine, a query sanitizer, an opt-in dry-run token for safe action simulators, and a safety harness that enforces rate/cost/side-effect limits. Key behaviors: deterministic replay using time-offsets, injected small-scale fuzzing of metric values to test threshold robustness, RBAC gating so only users with `rehearsal.run` can execute live-like scenarios, and a canary gating step that requires a staged approval for any experiment that includes write-side effects. The description below lists changes, checks, and rollout plan. Checklist: - [x] telemetry ingestion slice and time-offset replay - [x] query sanitizer that strips identifiers and rewrites agg windows - [x] dry-run token and simulated action driver - [x] safety harness with cost/rate caps and write-effect blockers - [x] UI controls in the incident-bot dashboard to create rehearsal snapshots - [x] unit + integration tests for replay determinism - [x] Linear link for tracking: ENG-5123 Deployment plan: feature-flagged for 2 weeks in staging, invite-only beta for SREs, then gradual enablement with audit logs and automatic revert on assertion failures. Known limitations: large trace replays are sampled to avoid runaway costs; external downstream hooks are stubbed in dry-run mode. Related work: builds on prior snapshot exporter PRs and the ephemeral-playbook architecture.
